items.title: Fold a signed storyFilesHash into the delivery-check signature
items.context: Add storyFilesHash?:string to DeliveryCheckData (core/types.ts); add the param to signDeliveryCheck + recomputeDeliveryCheckHash (core/delivery-check-hash.ts); compute currentStoryFilesHash and persist+sign it in delivery_check_set AND the delivery_waiver_add re-sign path (handlers/delivery-check.ts). Legacy records without storyFilesHash must recompute byte-identically.

happy.desc: signDeliveryCheck with storyFilesHash present produces a signature that covers the storyFilesHash value; recomputeDeliveryCheckHash with the same storyFilesHash reproduces the identical hash -> signature verification passes; WHY: confirms storyFilesHash is actually inside the signed payload

delivery_check_set computes currentStoryFilesHash and persists it in the written record alongside the signature -> stored record.storyFilesHash is non-empty and record._hash verifies; WHY: confirms the writer path actually stores and signs the field

delivery_waiver_add re-sign path preserves storyFilesHash from the original delivery-check through the waiver re-sign -> re-signed record.storyFilesHash equals original; WHY: confirms the waiver path does not lose the field

edge.desc: Legacy delivery-check record with no storyFilesHash field -> recomputeDeliveryCheckHash produces byte-identical hash to the original legacy _hash; WHY: append-only signature payload must not break existing records
storyFilesHash is empty string (edge vs null/undefined) -> treated as missing (legacy path), not as a valid hash; WHY: empty-string sentinel must not create a forgeable match

adversarial.desc: Forged storyFilesHash: attacker edits the stored record to set storyFilesHash to a value that matches currentStoryFilesHash but was NOT in the original signature -> recomputeDeliveryCheckHash returns a hash that does NOT match _hash (tampered); WHY: the core security invariant -- unsigned storyFilesHash must not be a forgeable bypass

Attacker removes storyFilesHash from a record that was originally signed WITH it -> recomputeDeliveryCheckHash(without storyFilesHash) differs from _hash (tampered); WHY: field deletion must also break the signature

verificationEvidence.note: delivery-check-freshness-smoke.ts:332-363 (forged storyFilesHash case) + :41-61 (signDeliveryCheck): signDeliveryCheck folds storyFilesHash into the sha256 payload (line 57); the smoke forges storyFilesHash on a real delivery record and asserts the re-computed hash differs from _hash (line 352-353), proving storyFilesHash is inside the signed payload. recomputeDeliveryCheckHash (line 67-78) passes the stored storyFilesHash through the same signDeliveryCheck path, so same-input reproduces identical hash. The first smoke case (line 212-244) does delivery_check_set which signs with storyFilesHash and then evaluateDeliveryCheckFreshness returns ok:true, confirming signature verification passes.

delivery-check-freshness-smoke.ts:212-244 (first case): deliveryCheckSet calls createDeliveryCheckHandlers then delivery_check_set (line 156-157), asserts "Delivery check saved" (line 163), reads the stored record (line 164), and asserts delivery.storyFilesHash is truthy via the advisory case (line 267). The record._hash is verified by evaluateDeliveryCheckFreshness returning ok:true (line 227). delivery-check-hash.ts signDeliveryCheck (line 41-61) folds storyFilesHash into the hash; recomputeDeliveryCheckHash (line 67-78) recomputes and matches _hash.

delivery-check.ts waiver re-sign path: the waiver_add handler calls signDeliveryCheck with the existing record fields including storyFilesHash. The smoke test delivery-check-freshness-smoke.ts does not have an explicit waiver case, but the signing function signDeliveryCheck (delivery-check-hash.ts:41-61) is shared by both delivery_check_set and waiver re-sign, and it preserves storyFilesHash when present (line 57). The handler reads the existing record, re-signs with its fields (including storyFilesHash), and writes back. Logic inspection confirms the waiver path does not strip or omit storyFilesHash from the re-sign call.

delivery-check-freshness-smoke.ts:366-393 (legacy case): legacyDeliveryCheck() (line 173-187) creates a record WITHOUT materialHash or storyFilesHash, calling signDeliveryCheck with no materialHash/storyFilesHash args. signDeliveryCheck (delivery-check-hash.ts:56-57) conditionally appends these only when present, so the legacy hash is computed without them. recomputeDeliveryCheckHash (line 67-78) reads the stored record (which has no storyFilesHash) and passes undefined, reproducing the identical legacy hash. The smoke asserts evaluateDeliveryCheckFreshness still works (returns stale_delivery_check, not tampered), confirming byte-identical recomputation.

delivery-check-hash.ts:56-57 signDeliveryCheck: storyFilesHash is appended to the payload ONLY when truthy ("...(storyFilesHash ? [storyFilesHash] : [])"). An empty string is falsy in JS, so it takes the [] branch — identical to undefined/null. evaluateDeliveryCheckFreshness (line 158) checks "if (deliveryCheck.storyFilesHash)" — empty string is falsy, so the advisory branch is never entered. The legacy stale path (line 173-180) applies. This means empty-string storyFilesHash is treated as missing (legacy), not as a valid hash that could forge a match.

delivery-check-freshness-smoke.ts:332-363 (forged storyFilesHash case): creates a real signed delivery record, then forges storyFilesHash to "f".repeat(64) (line 339). Asserts that re-signing with the forged value produces a DIFFERENT hash from the original _hash (line 347-353). Writes the forged record to the store and asserts done-oracle returns status=fail with _hash mismatch detail (line 357-358) and machine guard blocks with delivery_check_tampered (line 360). This proves an unsigned storyFilesHash forgery is detected because the signature covers it.

delivery-check-hash.ts:50-61 signDeliveryCheck: storyFilesHash is conditionally appended (line 57). If a record was signed WITH storyFilesHash (truthy), removing it changes the payload (one fewer element in the join). recomputeDeliveryCheckHash (line 67-78) reads whatever is on the stored record — if storyFilesHash was deleted, it passes undefined, the payload shrinks, and the recomputed hash differs from _hash. The smoke forged-storyFilesHash case (delivery-check-freshness-smoke.ts:332-363) proves the signature mechanism catches field changes; deletion is a subset of that (changing from a value to undefined), and the conditional-append logic (line 56-57) guarantees the payload changes in both directions.

items.title: Add the drift-advisory downgrade branch to evaluateDeliveryCheckFreshness
items.context: core/delivery-check-hash.ts: on materialHash mismatch, if a signed storyFilesHash matches currentStoryFilesHash, return ok:true code delivery_check_drift_advisory with a mandatory advisory and never rebind the stored hash; missing or mismatched storyFilesHash keeps strict stale_delivery_check.

happy.desc: materialHash mismatch + SIGNED storyFilesHash equals currentStoryFilesHash -> evaluateDeliveryCheckFreshness returns {ok:true, code:"delivery_check_drift_advisory", advisory:"<non-empty string>"} and stored hash is NOT rebound; WHY: the core happy-path downgrade that eliminates the re-sign friction
materialHash matches (fresh) -> returns ok:true code fresh regardless of storyFilesHash; WHY: the existing fresh path must not regress

edge.desc: materialHash mismatch + storyFilesHash is missing/null (legacy record) -> strict stale_delivery_check (ok:false); WHY: legacy records without storyFilesHash must never get the advisory downgrade
materialHash mismatch + storyFilesHash present but currentStoryFilesHash is empty (HEAD on main, no story branch) -> strict stale; WHY: empty currentStoryFilesHash should not match a real stored hash

adversarial.desc: materialHash mismatch + SIGNED storyFilesHash does NOT match currentStoryFilesHash (story-owned file changed) -> strict stale_delivery_check (ok:false); WHY: a story-owned change must never be downgraded to an advisory

Record has _hash tampered (storyFilesHash was forged post-signature) -> recomputeDeliveryCheckHash mismatch -> delivery_check_tampered BEFORE the freshness branch even runs; WHY: signature verification must precede any advisory logic

Concurrent main merge during evaluateDeliveryCheckFreshness: currentStoryFilesHash computed at call time vs currentMaterialHash are from the same git snapshot -> no TOCTOU race between the two computations; WHY: if storyFilesHash and materialHash are computed at different git states, a mid-merge could cause a false advisory

verificationEvidence.note: delivery-check-freshness-smoke.ts:253-302 (non-story whole-tree drift case): after deliveryCheckSet, merges an unrelated main change into the story branch. Asserts materialHash changed (line 281), storyFilesHash unchanged (line 282). evaluateDeliveryCheckFreshness returns ok:true, code delivery_check_drift_advisory, advisory=EXPECTED_ADVISORY (lines 286-288). Line 289 asserts the stored materialHash is NOT rebound (still equals delivery.materialHash). This covers the exact intent: materialHash mismatch + signed storyFilesHash match -> advisory downgrade, no rebind.

delivery-check-freshness-smoke.ts:212-244 (first case): deliveryCheckSet writes a fresh delivery-check, then evaluateDeliveryCheckFreshness returns ok:true (line 227) and doneRow status=pass (line 228). No materialHash mismatch exists (line 226 confirms afterMaterial==delivery.materialHash). The storyFilesHash is present on the record (confirmed by advisory case line 267) but irrelevant here because materialHash matches — the function returns delivery_check_passed at line 183-190 without ever entering the storyFilesHash branch.

items.title: Surface the advisory loudly on the DONE delivery-check row
items.context: core/done-oracle.ts: delivery_check_drift_advisory passes the gate (status pass) but appends the mandatory advisory to the row detail, never swallowed.

happy.desc: delivery_check_drift_advisory result from evaluateDeliveryCheckFreshness -> done-oracle delivery-check row has status=pass AND row.detail contains the literal advisory text (e.g. "whole-tree materialHash drift detected" or equivalent); WHY: the advisory must be VISIBLE on the passing DONE row, never swallowed
Normal fresh delivery-check -> done-oracle row status=pass with standard detail (no advisory appended); WHY: the advisory path must not pollute the normal fresh path

edge.desc: Advisory text is appended to existing detail, not replacing it -> row.detail contains BOTH the original N-docs-promises text AND the advisory; WHY: existing detail must not be clobbered
delivery_check_drift_advisory with an advisory string that contains special characters (newlines, quotes) -> row.detail is not truncated or corrupted; WHY: advisory text fidelity

adversarial.desc: Tampered delivery-check (_hash mismatch) -> done-oracle row status=fail with tampered detail, NOT pass with advisory; WHY: tampered must never be downgraded to advisory

Stale delivery-check (story-owned change, storyFilesHash mismatch) -> done-oracle row status=fail with stale detail, NOT pass with advisory; WHY: story-owned drift must still hard-reject at the DONE gate

An attacker crafts a delivery-check record with code=delivery_check_drift_advisory but the _hash does not verify -> done-oracle recomputes and finds tampered, row=fail; WHY: the code field alone must not bypass signature verification

items.title: Re-fixture delivery-check-freshness smoke to story-branch topology and add the drift cases
items.context: packages/main/src/tasks/delivery-check-freshness-smoke.ts: HEAD ahead of main so currentStoryFilesHash is non-empty; cases for non-story whole-tree drift -> advisory pass, story-owned change -> stale reject, forged storyFilesHash -> tampered, legacy missing storyFilesHash -> strict stale. Reference /tmp/friction1-cfresh-fix/redgreen-spike-test.ts.

happy.desc: Smoke fixture puts HEAD ahead of main (story-branch topology) -> currentStoryFilesHash is non-empty; non-story whole-tree drift case -> advisory pass; smoke asserts the LITERAL advisory text on the passing DONE row detail (not just the code path); WHY: the product-reviewer recommendation -- assert the actual user-visible advisory wording, not just ok:true
Story-owned change case -> stale reject; smoke asserts the DONE row status=fail with stale detail; WHY: story-owned drift must be a pinned rejection
Forged storyFilesHash case -> tampered (_hash breaks); smoke asserts the DONE row status=fail with tampered detail; WHY: forgery detection is pinned
Legacy missing storyFilesHash case -> strict stale; smoke asserts the DONE row status=fail; WHY: legacy records must stay strict

edge.desc: node packages/main/dist/tasks/delivery-check-freshness-smoke.js exits 0 AND npm test (root) is green -> no regressions from the re-fixturing; WHY: the smoke rewrite must not break other smokes

Smoke cases are isolated from each other (each case sets up its own fixture state, not shared mutable state) -> case ordering does not affect results; WHY: flaky ordering-dependent tests are a known failure mode

adversarial.desc: Smoke drift-advisory case asserts the hash is NOT rebound after the advisory pass -> the stored materialHash in the delivery-check record is still the OLD value; WHY: rebinding would silently accept the drift and break future staleness detection

An attacker adds a 5th case to the smoke that always passes regardless of input (vacuous test) -> code review catches it because each case must assert a SPECIFIC code/status/detail triple, not just exit 0; WHY: vacuous tests undermine the smoke suite

items.title: Amend the spec and process-fact rationale and add the Gate-A keep-strict note
items.context: docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md DONE Sub-Gate amendment (B strict, C adopt-with-signed-guard, A excluded-frozen-ref); update delivery_check_set rationale in core/process-fact-levels.ts + core/process-fact-registry.ts; add a code comment at done-oracle.ts checkCompletedEvidenceSnapshotFreshness that storyFilesHash is intentionally not applied (frozen-ref integrity check).

happy.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/story-files-hash-material-drift.md contains a DONE Sub-Gate Bindings section that records: Gate A excluded (frozen-ref integrity), Gate B kept strict, Gate C adopt-with-signed-guard -> grep/read confirms the three bindings with rationale; WHY: the spec is the canonical design record

node scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs exits 0 -> process-fact-levels + process-fact-registry are consistent after the rationale update; WHY: the contract verifier is the ground truth for process-fact consistency

done-oracle.ts checkCompletedEvidenceSnapshotFreshness has a code comment stating storyFilesHash is intentionally not applied (frozen-ref integrity check) -> grep confirms the comment; WHY: prevents future cargo-cult wire-in of storyFilesHash into Gate A

edge.desc: process-fact-registry delivery_check_set rationale mentions both signed storyFilesHash AND drift-advisory semantics -> rationale is not stale/generic; WHY: rationale must be specific to the new behavior, not a leftover
npm --prefix packages/main run build exits 0 -> no TypeScript errors from the spec/rationale/comment changes; WHY: doc-comment or string changes can cause TS errors if they break template literals

adversarial.desc: Spec amendment does NOT claim Gate A or Gate B are downgraded -> grep for storyFilesHash in the A/B sections confirms they say excluded/strict, not adopt; WHY: a copy-paste error could accidentally document a downgrade that does not exist in code

Gate-A keep-strict comment is inside the actual function body (not in an unrelated file or dead code) -> the comment is co-located with the frozen-ref integrity check logic; WHY: a comment in the wrong place provides no cargo-cult protection
